Access tailored resources, pricing models, and support levels. GS Caltex uses Amazon SageMaker Canvas and Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to connect process engineers’ models to production workflows. The South Korean energy and chemical company divides model development and operations between engineers with complementary skills. Process engineers build and validate models in SageMaker Canvas without writing code, drawing on their process knowledge. Machine learning (ML) engineers configure SageMaker Pipelines workflows for deployment and scheduled inference. Moving assets from SageMaker Canvas into SageMaker Pipelines still required integration work. ML engineers had to set data paths for production, supply the model configuration, and connect preprocessing and inference jobs. GS Caltex automated this handoff while reusing the assets created in SageMaker Canvas. GS Caltex reports that its ML engineers now deploy models within a few hours, compared with about a week before. The company runs batch inference every 30 minutes, reducing the need for continuously running endpoints. GS Caltex reports that this has meaningfully lowered its inference costs. This post explains how GS Caltex connects SageMaker Canvas to SageMaker Pipelines and reuses validated preprocessing flows and models in production. The machine learning operations (MLOps) workflow has two paths: preparing a new model version for deployment, and running batch inference with the deployed model. You can use SageMaker Canvas to prepare data visually, build models, and generate batch predictions. You can also register validated models in Amazon SageMaker Model Registry from SageMaker Canvas. GS Caltex built a separate handoff process to turn these assets into executable SageMaker Pipelines steps. Process engineers understand the variables and data behind a process and assess whether a model’s predictions are useful. ML engineers turn the resulting assets into production jobs and manage model versions and execution history. The following diagram shows how process engineers hand off SageMaker Canvas assets to ML engineers for deployment and scheduled inference. ML engineers use Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) for preprocessing flows and Model Registry for model versions, then schedule pipeline runs through Amazon EventBridge. Figure 1: SageMaker Canvas assets connected to a SageMaker Pipelines workflow for scheduled batch inference ML engineers receive the preprocessing flow and model from SageMaker Canvas and review the data formats and prediction results. After that review, they approve the model in Model Registry and deploy it. This preparation takes place when a new model version is deployed. Subsequent inference runs reuse the deployed model. Amazon EventBridge starts each scheduled run. SageMaker Pipelines prepares the input data from Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), runs preprocessing and SageMaker Batch Transform, and stores the results in S3. ML engineers can inspect step status and Amazon CloudWatch logs to monitor the workflow. The production pipeline reuses the preprocessing logic and trained model created in SageMaker Canvas. ML engineers configure the input and output paths, set the order of execution, and write the code that connects approval and scheduling to the workflow. The full reference implementation is available in the GitHub repository. The code examples in this post focus on the connections between components. The repository uses a sample loan classification model, so adjust the configuration to match your model’s input and output formats. The following steps cover preprocessing reuse, model approval and deployment, pipeline construction, and scheduled inference. A preprocessing flow created with Data Wrangler in SageMaker Canvas records the data sources and transformation steps. To set up the reference implementation, export data to Amazon S3 using SageMaker Processing, then retrieve the job settings and the .flow file used by that job. In the export settings, turn off Auto job configuration and select SageMaker Processing. After the export starts, open the Processing job details on the Amazon SageMaker AI console. Record the container image URI, the S3 URI of the input named flow, the execution role, and the output settings. Use these values to configure the pipeline step that runs the .flow file. The SageMaker execution role must have permissions to read the required S3 data, write the results, and access the container image. Choose the instance type and count based on the volume of data you need to process. Keep the preprocessing logic validated by the process engineer, and adjust the data sources, paths, and other settings for the production environment. Check the container image and output node against the original job configuration. Some .flow files contain execution metadata such as internal_metadata.dw_job.container_uri. Check the actual Processing job settings rather than assuming that every export contains this field. If you move the workflow to another AWS Region, verify that the container image is available there. The reference implementation separates intermediate and final outputs by execution under runs/<execution-id>/. Its PrepareInput step writes data to a fixed S3 location referenced by the .flow file. Prevent executions that share that input path from overlapping. To isolate input data for each execution as well, add a preparation step that updates the source URI in a copy of the .flow file. Declaring a SageMaker Pipelines parameter does not automatically replace a URI inside the file. The target column is one difference between training and inference data. A flow built with training data can contain transformations that expect the target column in the input schema. Inference data does not contain that known outcome. The reference implementation adds a PrepareInput step before preprocessing. If the target column is missing, this step adds it with a placeholder value. After preprocessing, DropTargetColumn removes the column. Match the placeholder’s data type and column position to the training schema, and pass only the expected features to the model in their original order. Use this approach only when the placeholder target does not affect feature values. A flow that filters rows by the target, derives features from it, or applies target encoding needs additional treatment. In those cases, separate the transformations and learned state required for inference. Validation should cover column order and count, data types, missing-value handling, and row count. After removing the target, check that the remaining columns match the feature order used during training. Register the validated SageMaker Canvas model version in Model Registry. The registered version can include the model files, inference configuration, and evaluation results. ML engineers review this information before changing the approval status. The model file, such as model.tar.gz, must be used with the correct inference container and environment settings. A model package in Model Registry groups this information together. In this batch architecture, deployment creates a SageMaker model resource from an approved package for Batch Transform to reference. The following example checks a package that has already been approved, then creates the model resource. Supply model_package_arn, model_name, and sagemaker_role_arn during deployment. This example uses a unique model name for each version. Model Registry records approval status, but it does not enforce an approval check on every inference request. Check that status in the deployment code and retain the selected package ARN and model name in the pipeline configuration. If approval is revoked, update the schedules and execution configurations that use the model. Registration and deployment take place when a model version is released. The pipeline that runs every 30 minutes creates Batch Transform jobs using that model, so it does not need to register the model again on each run. Configure each job before connecting the steps. In the following example, prepare_args, preprocess_args, drop_target_args, and assemble_args hold the step arguments returned by run() calls on processors that use a PipelineSession. The processors and transformer share the pipeline_session object. Configure the transformer with the previously deployed model_name. The following execution graph shows the five steps in the sample loan model’s inference workflow. They prepare inputs, apply preprocessing, remove the target column, run batch inference, and assemble results. The execution was in the Executing state when this screenshot was taken. Figure 2: SageMaker Pipelines execution graph for the sample loan model Use depends_on to control execution order, and pass data through step output properties. For example, assemble_args must receive the location of the preprocessed data and predict.properties.TransformOutput.S3OutputPath. The output name "features" belongs to DropTargetColumn. The Data Wrangler step uses the output ID defined in its preprocessing flow. In the reference implementation, AssembleResults combines the preprocessed data and predictions by row position. Before using it in production, add checks that file order and row counts match, and stop result generation if they do not. If preprocessing sorts or removes rows, maintain an explicit mapping between source record IDs and predictions. GS Caltex runs inference every 30 minutes. The following example uses an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule SageMaker Pipelines executions. Create the pipeline and verify it with a manual run before attaching the schedule. Set eventbridge_role_arn to a role that trusts the Amazon EventBridge service principal, events.amazonaws.com, and has sagemaker:StartPipelineExecution permission for the target pipeline. The pipeline_arn value identifies the pipeline created in the previous step. The expression rate(30 minutes) schedules runs at 30-minute intervals. To run on the hour and half hour, use cron(0/30 * * * ? *). Decide which data window each run processes in the input preparation step, and record it with the execution. Before enabling scheduled runs, check the total cost, execution time, and handling of invalid or mismatched data. Amazon SageMaker Pipelines is a serverless workflow orchestration service. It manages execution order and dependencies without a workflow server for you to provision or maintain. Processing and Batch Transform jobs use separate compute resources and are billed according to instance type and duration. A provisioned real-time endpoint is a good fit for requests that need a consistently low-latency response. Batch Transform suits workloads that can process a set of records together. It releases the job’s compute resources when the job finishes, so you can run predictions without keeping an inference endpoint running continuously for each model. A 30-minute schedule produces 48 scheduled runs per day. Include preprocessing, instance startup, inference, and postprocessing when estimating total runtime. The cost comparison should also account for Processing, S3, CloudWatch, and other services used by the workflow. Assess the cost of each workload using its measured usage, including the supporting services and the full runtime of every scheduled job. A schedule that starts a run every 30 minutes does not guarantee that each run finishes within that interval. Measure the full pipeline runtime with representative data, including instance startup and the time needed to retry failed jobs. Decide how to handle a scheduled run that arrives before the previous execution has finished. Controlling parallel steps within a pipeline does not prevent separate pipeline executions from overlapping. Check active executions, prevent duplicate processing of the same input window, and separate the output paths for each run. Record the input data window, preprocessing flow version, model package ARN, pipeline execution ARN, and output location for each run. These details help reproduce results and investigate errors. Complete the following checks before you enable the schedule: Add CloudWatch alerts for job failures and processing delays, together with data quality or model monitoring as needed. Set initial thresholds from measured runtime and data characteristics, and review them when the model or data volume changes. With a staged rollout, a team can verify the handoff before standardizing it across models. The following sections describe an adoption approach and the results GS Caltex reported. Start by validating the path to production for one model, then standardize the steps that repeat across deployments. The following sequence is a suggested adoption approach based on the GS Caltex experience. As automation expands, process engineers continue to assess whether the predictions are useful for the process. ML engineers manage pipeline execution and changes. GS Caltex reduced the repeated work needed to connect SageMaker Canvas models to production. ML engineers now deploy models within a few hours, compared with about a week previously. They also reuse the assets that process engineers validated in SageMaker Canvas. Process engineers began proposing applications in other processes after seeing their models used in production. ML engineers spent less time repeating integration work and could focus on operating and monitoring the pipelines. For a test deployment, disable the Amazon EventBridge rule and remove its targets first. After active pipeline executions and jobs have finished, delete the test pipeline and its SageMaker model resources. If you created a real-time endpoint for testing, delete it as well. Remove input, intermediate, and prediction files from S3, and clean up CloudWatch logs according to your retention policy. Check whether other executions or audit requirements still depend on model files and Model Registry versions before deleting them. At GS Caltex, process engineers create and validate models in SageMaker Canvas, and ML engineers use those assets to run production workflows in SageMaker Pipelines. This handoff reduced repeated integration work. GS Caltex reports that ML engineers now complete model deployments within a few hours, compared with about a week before. The handoff needs to include the preprocessing flow, input schema, inference configuration, and approval process alongside the model files. Verify that the workflow reproduces the expected results and can run reliably on the required schedule. To try this approach, start with one model you have validated in SageMaker Canvas and use the GitHub repository. See the SageMaker Pipelines developer guide for details on defining and running workflows. Check preprocessing and batch prediction results with a manual execution, then schedule runs at the interval your application needs. In part 2, we show how GS Caltex used Amazon Bedrock to automate moving existing models onto this pipeline. WonGu is a Data Analyst at GS Caltex’s DAX Lab. He specializes in data analysis, machine learning model development and operations, model performance optimization, and MLOps. In addition, he drives operational efficiency and data-informed decision-making for business teams by designing and integrating enterprise AI agents, workflows, and data pipelines. Hyunsoo is a Senior APJ GTM Specialist Solutions Architect for GenAI at Amazon Web Services. Based in Seoul, he helps customers across Asia Pacific design generative AI solutions, including AI agents, advanced RAG, model optimization, and MLOps. Sang is a Senior Account Executive at AWS Korea. He helps customers in the energy and manufacturing industries adopt cloud technologies and put AI into practice. He works with AWS specialists and partners to support customers from proof of concept through production deployment and broader adoption. Joonhyung is a Senior Solutions Architect and a physical AI and spatial computing specialist at AWS Korea. He helps customers build and operate digital twin, 3D, and AR/VR/XR applications on AWS, with a focus on delivery speed and cost efficiency. His experience spans generative AI, machine learning, data, and cloud architecture.

title: How Will Higher-than-Expected Inflation Data Impact the Fed's Next Rate Decisions? - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. While a smaller hike remains more likely, October’s hotter-than-expected inflation data may open the door to a 50-basis point rate hike at the Fed’s December meeting, says Muhammad Qubbaj, co-head of North America Interest Rate Product Sales and Trading in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. A recent drop in oil prices is unlikely to give the Fed cover to look past the CPI number without becoming more aggressive in the inflation fight, Qubbaj says on this episode of The Markets podcast. He also explains why his base case is for the 10-Year Treasury yield to remain below recent highs. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Thursday, November 12th, and we're here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Muhammad Qubbaj, who is co-head of North American Interest Rate Sales and Trading within FICC and Equities. And today, we're going to talk about how a hot CPI print this week is impacting rates and bonds markets, and how that has a carryover effect to other markets around the world. Chris Hussey: Okay, Q, let's start with the CPI print. It came in hot this week. What did you make of the market's reaction? How do you think the Fed is going to respond? Muhammad Qubbaj: Well, there's no rest for the wicked when you look at the sources of volatility in the market, whether it's geopolitics, whether it's the Fed, whether it's AI. We felt we almost had a little bit of a respite, maybe for five minutes, and all of a sudden CPI comes to the forefront and changes the board a little bit, too, and the Fed walks right back into the building. CPI affected us in three ways. First, I would say that it was unacceptable number, .3, third time in a row. Strong across all categories. The Fed has to reckon with that number, and the market priced that accordingly. Two, it wasn't just about the CPI level, it was about the Fed reaction function. We woke up that morning, Waller had made a speech and put 50s back on the table. He basically asked a question, and CPI answered. He said, "Contingent on .3, 50s could be on the table." And- Chris Hussey: And by 50s on the table, what you mean is that we could do a hike of 50 basis points, not 25. Muhammad Qubbaj: Exactly. So it just, again, underscored a hawkishness to the Fed and opened up the distribution to 50s, which was definitely a surprise that morning, before we even walked in and got the CPI number. The third thing was we spent almost a month executing a hike compression. We took out almost 50 basis points of hikes in the next one year, and some of this is a give back. So in terms of the market reaction, unwind of positioning and the high compression, a reaction to the strength of the CPI, the third one in a row and a re-understanding of the Fed's reaction function and opening up the distribution for 50s. Chris Hussey: All right, so it wasn't trivial. That's interesting. But you also talk about a Fed reaction function, and one of the things they have to react to is oil, I would imagine, because, this was an October report, but for the month of November, oil prices are now down 15%. How does oil factor into the rates market? Muhammad Qubbaj: We can't basically say that the causality between oil and rates is a one-for-one thing. They're definitely a participant. They definitely have a feed through to CPI, and they definitely show up into, basically, core CPI and how the Fed takes that number so that they can adjust policy. But, the sell-off wasn't just about oil when we had the big sell-off in the year. At one point it was about corporate earnings and growth. At another point it was a debate on the Fed reaction function uncertainty because they removed forward guidance term premium on the back of bond supply and CapEx supply, convexity hedging or the convexity profile of the market where we saw a lot of selling and positioning. Oil coming off in the last couple of weeks is definitely affects the level of rates, but you can't expect a full refund just based on the oil movement. Chris Hussey: Okay. Another thing that's changed since that October CPI print was the midterms. We got the midterms in early November. How does a change in Congress, if at all, have any impact on the rates market? Muhammad Qubbaj: I think a couple of things. One is the Fed's not a political body. It should not affect the Fed path, first order. It affects oil, obviously, based on the vote on the geopolitical outlook of the Iran war. Midterms affect oil, CPI affects the Fed. We've had almost triple the move based on the CPI morning print that we did in rates for the entire of midterms week. So I think that's where the focus is. Chris Hussey: Okay, Q, let's expand the conversation to 10-year bond yields. They have such an impact across markets. We were up at 5.3% not too long ago. They've come back to 5%. Are the conditions still in place, though, for us to eclipse the recent highs? Muhammad Qubbaj: You have to look at basically what took us to the peak in rates. There were several different factors. One, we had this new reaction function from the Fed, no forward guidance, the debate on how the Fed's reaction function will evolve under a Warsh leadership. You had the debate on term premium. You had the debate on Government issuance compounded by AI CapEx-related supply. You had a positioning situation in the market. You also had convexity selling in the market. All of those things contributed to the sell-off. So, I don't think that you're going to have that same set of circumstances reassert itself on the market again and push yields to the high, high level that we saw in October. Furthermore, you have two new breaks in the system: a Fed that is actively hiking, a hike lands in the front end but flattens the curve. Two, we had some sort of reflexivity that's been put onto the market in Warsh's last speech. He specifically tied the level of rates to the level of AI CapEx financing. So what happens when you do that is basically saying that you have a self-balancing system. If rates go up too much, then it can slow down the AI CapEx build-out, and it will almost have a self-balancing system from that perspective. But let us remember that if -- Do I think it's going to be a rate sell-off can happen again driven by positioning or term premium or supply worries or convexity selling? No. If we have a reassertion of strong earnings and I think that can give us some room. Chris Hussey: Yeah, a little bit of a growth-driven thing. Can I ask you to define one thing? Convexity selling, what is that? Muhammad Qubbaj: Convexity selling is a situation where, as the market sells off, people have more to sell. At its core, it means as things are getting worse, your flows are going to make it even worse. Chris Hussey: Right. It's a little technical factor. All right, let's talk about the competition between stocks, bonds, and credit. Cause that's always part of the equation here, I would imagine. How do you see that shaping up here? You talked about the growth equation being such a big one for where yields go from here. Muhammad Qubbaj: When we look at yields as it pertains to credit and as it pertains to equities, we have to look at it from a couple of lenses. What drives higher yields? Is it growth? Is it earnings? Then that should be good for the credit complex, and should be good for the equity complex. Is it driven by term premium worries and a supply absorption worries? Then you have a capital markets problem, and that's where they could be negative for equities, and it could be negative for credit. That's one factor. The other factor is the amount of leverage that we're talking about. When you're looking at a bond that is a corporation that is on the lower side of the spectrum of leverage, then higher rates affects the discount factor. When you look at a bond that's on the other side of the leverage spectrum, higher rates is a funding bill. It's a funding problem. So you can't... You have to be a little bit more nuanced when you say how do higher rates affect the equity market or credit market. It's a function of how did we get there, and how levered are the companies that we're talking about?  And that's basically where you get your answer. Chris Hussey: All right, lot to digest. Let's put a bow on it. What's the trade? Muhammad Qubbaj: I like to think of it from a serenity prayer perspective. Muhammad Qubbaj: Accept the things you cannot change. It is a one-factor market. It's all about mega-cap tech. Once you accept that, you realize that's the bet you're going to be making. Now, where do you have control? Where can you make some changes on the edges? One is how much of a size of a position you're going to take. It depends on how you hedge your portfolio. Two, the amount of leverage and what's the expression you take on mega cap to see basically how much exposure you have and how much factor risk you have. So we have discussed the risk. Now let's discuss the hedges. When you look at the hedges, you basically have out-of-the-money dollar puts. You have out-of-the-money equity puts. Delta one is favorable in the level of rates. A combination of those, you can build a carry neutral or positive carry hedge portfolio, and you can size it up and down depending on the amount of risk and leverage you're taking on the mega-cap tech. Now, you wanna own the factor, and you wanna rent the insurance. Chris Hussey: And by owning the factor, you want to own stocks. Chris Hussey: And by renting the insurance, you wanna maybe own some puts as well. Chris Hussey: All right, what are you looking for in the weeks ahead? Muhammad Qubbaj: Three sources of volatility we mentioned in the market. Oil, let's continue to see how the geopolitical, situation unfolds. The Fed, we are going to look at Fed speak and the Fed minutes and basically try to read the tea leaves and to see how hawkish the Fed is right now so we can get a feeling for the size. While, we're confident on the direction of which way the Fed is going. It's about size and timing right now. And the third factor is the AI economy. Anything, whether it's a capital market situation or an earning situation, anything that can continue to give us confidence or allow us to re-rate the level of risk in the market as it pertains to the AI economy. Chris Hussey: That's terrific. Q, you're always just a fountain of knowledge for us. Really appreciate you joining us. Chris Hussey: That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. Safe Haven’s 16th Annual Dancing with the Statesboro Stars is set for Friday, Nov. 20 at Connection Church. Friday’s show is set for 6:30 p.m. Tickets, which are selling fast, are available online at https://www.etix.com/ticket/o/11901/DWTSS. Tickets will be available at the door. The annual fundraiser helps Safe Haven’s mission to assist victims of domestic violence and raises awareness about a subject that is sometimes kept in the dark. This year’s event is presented by D&R Intensive Car Care, said Kim Billings, director of Public Relations/Legal Services for Safe Haven, along with dozens of other sponsors. She also works to produce the Dancing with the Statesboro Stars show each year, alongside many other dedicated individuals, she said. “The DWTSS Committee and Safe Haven team work diligently behind the scenes to prepare for the much-loved community event,” Billings said. “We are so grateful for all for volunteers, sponsors and community support that goes into making this such a success.” While the event is fun to watch and for the participants on stage, the fundraiser helps to meet the needs of Safe Haven and assist local victims of domestic violence. Safe Haven’s mission is “…to serve, strengthen and support victims and children of domestic violence through the provision of emergency and community-based services. Safe Haven is dedicated to ending the cycle of family violence through prevention, education, outreach and housing programs,” Billings said. “The DWTSS annual fundraiser is vital to Safe Haven,” Billings said. “Financial assistance provided by our agency includes utility deposits, rental assistance, legal assistance, and other needed necessities to support an independent life free from abuse.” She added, “This event has also become an entertaining way to raise awareness about a topic a lot of people either don’t want to talk about or don’t know enough about.” What the community may not realize about Safe Haven and its services, Billings said, is that all the services offered are free, as well as confidential. Phone calls made to the crisis line are answered 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. In 2024, the organization received 5,062 calls – an average of 14 calls per day. “We offer services to the men, women, children and pets that have experienced domestic violence,” she said. “Services include our 24/7 crisis line, safety planning, emergency shelter, temporary protective orders, outreach assistance, housing program, pet assistance and so much more.” In 2024, 699 individuals and 32 pets received direct assistance from Safe Haven. Also, Safe Haven provided 23,000 nights of emergency shelter and 14,350 meals in 2024. The service area includes six counties: Bulloch, Candler, Effingham, Jenkins, Screven and Washington.

title: GS Yuasa stock rebounded after full-year forecast upgrade - ad-hoc-news.de
content: GS Yuasa stock rebounded in Tokyo on November 9 after the company raised its full-year earnings outlook following strong first-half performance. Jiji Press reported that the shares briefly reached JPY 4,410, up JPY 207 from the previous trading day, after GS Yuasa announced the revision on November 6. For the fiscal year ending March 2027, GS Yuasa raised its operating profit forecast to JPY 66.5 billion from JPY 63.0 billion. The ordinary profit forecast increased to JPY 63.5 billion from JPY 61.0 billion, while projected net profit rose to JPY 41.0 billion from JPY 39.5 billion. The company kept its full-year sales forecast at JPY 680 billion. Jiji Press attributed the stronger outlook to the expectation that the mobility segment's first-half performance would continue into the second half. Market participants cited by Jiji Press also pointed to GS Yuasa's medium-term operating profit target of JPY 65 billion for fiscal 2028. The company reaching that target earlier than planned could support a further revision of its medium-term plan, according to the market commentary carried by the agency. title: Jon Bon Jovi names his favorite Italian restaurant in NJ. Here’s where it is - Asbury Park Press
content: It is always exciting to see local chefs and restaurants on television, and this week, three were given air time. One was praised by a legendary New Jersey rocker, another wowed a late-night host with its cheesesteak, and the third made a return to the Food Network. Victor Rallo's Italian restaurant, Undici, got a shoutout from Jon Bon Jovi, who shared his love of the eatery on the weekly Netflix video podcast "We’re Back! With Brian Williams." The program features Williams, a New Jersey native who spent some of his childhood years in Middletown, "in wide-ranging conversation with some of the most interesting figures shaping popular culture today," according to Netflix. On a recent episode, he asked the rocker to name the best Italian restaurant in Central Jersey "The best restaurant in Central New Jersey is a place called Undici," Bon Jovi said. "The man who opened it, the reason he opened it is he was looking for true fine dining in a place where he could go and get a table. So he opened his own restaurant, and thank God he did." Williams also gave a shoutout to Freehold Township ice cream shop and restaurant, Jersey Freeze, where Bon Jovi has been spotted with Bruce Springsteen. Go: Undici, 11 West River Road, Rumson; 732-842 3880, undicirestaurant.com A New York City-born cheesesteak shop with a Jersey Shore connection was featured on the Nov. 9 episode of "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon." Guest Pete Davidson, an actor and comedian know from his time on "Saturday Night Live," shared that he recently invested in G's Cheesesteaks, which has a restaurant in Toms River. Owners Jack Pisano, Derek Booras and Antonio Locke were in the audience. "These guys that I went to high school with in Staten Island … have a place directly across from (Madison Square Garden), and the cheesesteaks are phenomenal" Davidson said. "And I was like hey, can I get in on this?" Davidson brought cheesesteaks for Fallon and his band, The Roots, to try. "Unbelievable," Fallon said after taking a bite of a cheesesteak. "I love it." Go: 1611 Route 37, Toms River; 973-741-0090, gscheesesteaks.com Britt Rescigno, a New Jersey native who gained a following on Long Beach Island before opening a restaurant out west, is competing on Food Network's "Tournament of Champions: All-Star Christmas." The show's second season, which premiered Nov. 8, airs at 8 p.m. Sundays. Rescigno is paired with pastry chef Ashley Holt for the competition, which pits 16 two-person teams of chefs who are competing for $100,000, plus money for charity. Rescigno, who got her start in the culinary world at her family's New Gretna restaurant, Allen's Clam Bar, has appeared on four seasons of "Tournament of Champions," as well as the holiday version of the show and "Beat Bobby Flay," "Chopped," "Guy's Grocery Games" and "Alex vs. America." title: Why European Companies Are Forecast to Have Robust Earnings Growth - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. European company earnings are growing rapidly—and at a faster pace than the euro area economy. The strong earnings have helped the stock market absorb higher bond yields, elevated energy prices, and subdued domestic economic growth, writes Sharon Bell, senior European equity strategist for Goldman Sachs Research, in a report. Our analysts expect earnings per share for the STOXX 600 index of European stocks to grow 18% in 2026 and 7% in 2027. Meanwhile, euro area nominal GDP is forecast to grow 3.3% in 2026 and 2.8% in 2027. “This raises an important question,” Bell writes. “Why are European earnings proving more resilient than the domestic economy would suggest?” Investors often use domestic GDP growth to gauge company earnings growth, Bell observes. “But this relationship is far from mechanical and can vary significantly over time,” she adds. For example, the two were roughly aligned in 2025 when euro area nominal GDP grew around 3.7% while STOXX 600 earnings growth was 2.4%. This year, though, earnings are expected to considerably outpace economic growth. (The STOXX 600 benchmark reflects a broader European footprint than the euro area, spanning companies domiciled in the UK, Switzerland, and Denmark, among others.) One possible reason why earnings of listed European companies appear to be decoupling from domestic economic growth could be the composition of sectors represented among Europe’s biggest stocks. “The equity market is a distorted mirror of the economy,” Bell writes. GDP measures value across the entire domestic economy, whereas aggregate market earnings reflect the profits of a concentrated group of large listed companies. For example, companies in the financial sector account for more than 30% of EURO STOXX earnings (an index of euro area stocks), but only 10% of euro area economic activity. Energy and technology are also more important to listed earnings, while real estate, retail, and industrials have much larger weights in the economy relative to the European stock market. Country exposure also helps to explain the divergence between European earnings and the domestic economy. Listed companies now generate most of their revenues outside their country of domicile, and the euro area’s share of STOXX 600 sales has fallen from more than 60% in 1990 to about one-third today. At the same time, exposure to the US, Asia, and emerging markets has increased steadily, Bell observes. “With more than half of STOXX 600 revenues now generated outside Europe, global rather than domestic growth is increasingly more relevant for listed companies.” Goldman Sachs Research captures this with sales-weighted GDP growth, which weights regional growth by the geographic breakdown of companies’ revenues in the prior year. This measure has exceeded euro area growth in most years since the early 2000s. It is also the dominant driver of earnings: A 1 percentage point acceleration is associated with roughly 10 percentage points of higher STOXX 600 EPS growth. Currency also matters. A weaker euro raises the translated value of overseas profits, a meaningful share of which is denominated in US dollars, and improves the competitiveness of European companies. Europe is a net energy importer, so higher prices squeeze households and raise corporate costs. But the economy's sensitivity to oil prices has declined as the euro area economy has become less dependent on oil. The market's composition also provides a cushion: companies involved in energy and basic resources benefit directly from higher commodity prices, while chemicals companies and many industrial companies can pass costs on to customers. The cushion may not last. Sustained high energy costs can weaken company profit margins as growth and pricing power fade. The negative impact of higher costs can take time to appear in margins: After the 2022 energy shock, earnings for energy companies rose quickly while easing supply bottlenecks supported autos and chemicals companies; six to 12 months later, earnings estimates for energy and chemicals companies began to fall as commodity prices normalized and cost pressure became more visible. The current Middle East shock could follow a similar sequence, with margins outside financials and commodities coming under pressure if demand slows and pricing power fades. Given that our economists do not expect significant changes in euro area economic growth momentum, Bell’s team is more cautious than the consensus of financial analysts when it comes to European companies’ profit margins. Goldman Sachs Research forecasts broadly flat margins for STOXX 600 companies until 2028 after financials and commodities are excluded. On the other hand, the consensus of analysts expects margins to expand by more than 100 basis points to 10.1% from 8.7%. title: The Global Economy Is Forecast to Grow 2.8% in 2027 as Oil Prices Decline - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Goldman Sachs Research expects steady global economic growth in 2027, as lower energy prices and still-strong capital expenditures in artificial intelligence (AI) outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy. Global GDP is predicted to increase 2.8% in 2027, up from 2.7% this year, Jan Hatzius, chief economist and head of Goldman Sachs Research, writes in a report. The economies of the US, Japan, and the UK are among those projected to grow faster than the consensus of economist estimates. As has been the case for the last several years, our economists are more optimistic than consensus on US economic expansion owing to resilient investment. They are more downbeat on the European growth outlook amid tighter financial conditions and their expectation that higher energy prices will start to bite this winter. Goldman Sachs Research also forecasts continued robust economic expansion in South Korea and Taiwan, reflecting another year of strong AI exports. While growth is expected to be solid, the risks to Goldman Sachs Research’s forecast for global GDP growth “are tilted to the downside,” Hatzius writes. Renewed escalation in the Iran war could result in another energy price surge. Large fiscal deficits could push up long-term yields more sharply, especially in France. AI capex could be lower than expected because of capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress, or weaker demand, and Hatzius also sees early signs that AI adoption is weighing on the job market. “We expect another year of solid but unremarkable GDP growth in 2027, but several of the impulses that shaped global growth in 2026 will look different,” Hatzius writes. How will oil and energy prices affect GDP growth in 2027? The headwind from the energy supply shock will likely flip next year as energy prices normalize. The baseline forecast from Goldman Sachs Research’s commodity strategists is that continued Middle East supply adaptation will lower Brent prices to $78 per barrel by the end of 2027, with a similar normalization in global prices for liquefied natural gas. At the same time, Goldman Sachs Research sees an ongoing drag from energy prices in Europe from delayed energy cost pass-through to consumers. How financial conditions and the fiscal outlook will affect GDP growth Lower energy prices should outweigh the effect of tighter financial conditions and a smaller fiscal impulse to GDP expansion in 2027, Hatzius writes. Goldman Sachs Research’s Financial Conditions Index implies a moderate drag on growth over the next few quarters. While our economists do not “expect meaningful fiscal consolidation” in 2027, the large fiscal expansions of the last few years are fading. The main exception is in Japan, where consumption tax cuts, increased defense spending, and the government’s investment plans are forecast to boost GDP growth by 0.7 percentage point. “We also expect modestly positive impulses in Germany and the US—where the Democratic victory in November’s US election suggests some of the spending cuts from the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act will be reversed,” Hatzius writes. Our economists project a continued fiscal drag in the UK that leaves the fiscal impulse in developed markets “only slightly positive.” Goldman Sachs Research expects AI capex to boost global economic growth again next year. Our analysts forecast that nominal global AI investment will rise to $1.8 trillion in 2027 from $1.1 trillion this year, mostly driven by an increase of over $500 billion in hardware spending in the US. The investment surge is projected to be frontloaded, with the year-over-year change in investment as a share of GDP peaking in the first half of 2027. “Even with the expected slowdown, the impact on GDP growth will be sizable,” Hatzius writes. Our economists estimate that AI investment will boost GDP growth by 0.4 percentage point globally. In the US, Goldman Sachs Research estimates AI investment will give a 0.6-percentage-point boost to "true" GDP growth after accounting for continued undercounting of semiconductor investment and chip-related intellectual property exports. The transition to an AI-enabled economy, meanwhile, is occurring in two phases, according to Goldman Sachs Research. The first phase involves an investment boom that raises both corporate profits and global GDP growth but features only limited productivity gains. The second phase involves less hardware investment but more business reorganization, as well as more substantial productivity gains and labor market disruption. Goldman Sachs Research has argued that AI is likely to displace some jobs and cause a temporary increase in the unemployment rate. Our economists’ baseline expectation is that AI adoption will only have a small effect on the labor market in 2027 and there will be more notable effects in 2028-2029. What is the outlook for China’s economic growth in 2027? Goldman Sachs Research forecasts China’s GDP to grow 4.5% in 2027, compared with the consensus estimate of 4.4%. This “reflects very robust expectations for Chinese exports and a further increase in China’s trade surplus,” Hatzius writes. By contrast, domestic demand growth is predicted to remain weak next year owing to a drag from the property sector and weak underlying consumer spending. This is expected to result in a modest headwind of 0.1 percentage point to the rest of the world’s GDP growth, with larger drags on growth in manufacturing-heavy economies such as Germany (headwind of 0.3 percentage point) and Central Europe (headwind of 0.2 percentage point). Under Goldman Sachs Research’s baseline commodity forecasts for a steady decline in energy prices next year, inflation should slow in 2027, Hatzius writes. The case for disinflation is particularly strong in the US because the price boosts from tariffs should fully drop out of the year-over-year inflation statistics next spring, he writes. With tariff effects fading and a much smaller inflation boost from the war in Iran, our economists expect core PCE inflation to slow to 2.4% at the end of 2027 from 3.2% at the end of 2026. “We forecast a steady decline in year-over-year core inflation in the US and a more delayed decline in other major economies once the energy price shock is fully digested,” Hatzius writes. What is the outlook for the Fed and other central banks in 2027? Goldman Sachs Research expects “incremental policy tightening” through early 2027 in most major economies, but its economic forecasts support a dovish view on rates next year. Central banks could either deliver gradual normalization cuts later in 2027 as inflation comes down, or they could pivot to cuts sooner if economic growth is slower than projected. The US Federal Reserve is expected to hike rates in December and March in response to lingering inflation pressures. But our economists say softer inflation data should allow the Fed to cut once in December 2027, followed by three more cuts in 2028 to a terminal rate of 3.25-3.5%. “Furthermore, we see more dovish rate risks in the US than in most other economies, both because US inflation drivers look more clearly temporary and because the US is most exposed to a downturn in the AI cycle,” Hatzius writes. Our economists’ views on other major developed markets also skew dovish. The European Central Bank is forecast to deliver its final hike in December, before starting to normalize back toward a 2.25% terminal rate in the fourth quarter of 2027. Goldman Sachs Research expects a final hike from the Bank of England to 4.25% in February before a hold for the remainder of 2027. Our economists forecast normalization cuts from the BoE to a 3.25% terminal rate, but not until 2028. “The main outlier to our forecast of only modest further policy tightening is Japan,” Hatzius writes. Goldman Sachs Research expects the Bank of Japan to hike rates by 25 basis points in December, reflecting recent communication from the central bank highlighting both upside inflation risks and the impact of higher global interest rates on the Japanese yen. With core CPI (excluding fresh food but including energy) likely to rise above 3.5% through next summer, our economists now expect that the BoJ will follow through with additional hikes in March and June for a terminal rate of 2%. With Christmas fast approaching, now is the time to think about what you're buying and where you're buying it. We're not asking you to give up Amazon or the big-box stores. We're simply asking you to give your local businesses a look before you click that "Buy Now" button. title: Rwanda Gov Starts Pilot Scheme Delivering Ready-Cooked Meals to Schools - KT PRESS -
content: RWAMAGANA, Rwanda – The Rwandan government has begun testing a centralised school meal system that prepares food in large quantities and delivers it to schools – a mechanism similar to ones operating in Japan and South Korea. The shift, says education ministry, is also aimed at reducing reliance on firewood, improving nutrition and lowering the cost of school feeding. The pilot launched Friday serves 15,014 students and 266 teachers across five public schools in Rwamagana District. Meals are prepared at a central kitchen and transported to the schools in electric vehicles, replacing the need for each institution to cook its own food. The facility, located at GS Bujyujyu in Muyumbu Sector, was inaugurated on Friday, November 13, by the Minister of State for Education, Claudette Irere, alongside representatives of Solid’Africa, the local social enterprise implementing the project. The arrangement follows a hub-and-spoke model also used in Japan, where municipal school lunch centres, known as kyushoku centres, prepare meals for distribution to several schools. Japan has developed this system alongside school-based kitchens as part of a nationwide school feeding programme. The model allows large quantities of food to be prepared in specialised facilities before being transported to schools. It also supports centralised nutritional planning and hygiene management. In Japan, school meals are considered part of education, with students often serving food to classmates and eating together in their classrooms. South Korea also has a nationwide school meal system, although its arrangements are not identical to Japan’s. Its schools generally retain responsibility for meal operations, while procurement and distribution systems can involve centralised institutions. Rwanda’s pilot adapts some of these principles to local conditions. Its five participating schools are GS Bujyujyu, GS Muyumbu, GS Muyumbu B, GS Murama and GS Gitagara. Speaking at the inauguration, Irere said access to nutritious meals was directly linked to children’s ability to learn and perform well in school. “Every child in Rwanda deserves a good education, and no child should have to sit through a lesson on an empty stomach,” she said. “Hunger makes learning harder. As we work to improve what children learn in school, we must also ensure they have the nourishment they need to make the most of every school day.” She thanked Solid’Africa, The Rockefeller Foundation and other partners for supporting investments in school feeding infrastructure. One of the main differences between Rwanda’s approach and older centralised school kitchen systems elsewhere is its emphasis on clean energy. The facility operates within a one-hour delivery radius of the five schools. It prepares meals and dispatches them in electric vehicles to ensure they reach students in time for lunch. Its energy system combines rooftop solar panels with electricity from the national grid. Industrial electric cooking equipment replaces traditional wood-burning stoves. The arrangement is expected to eliminate harmful smoke from cooking facilities and reduce energy costs per meal. It also supports Rwanda’s target of phasing out biomass cooking in public institutions by 2030. Centralising food preparation could also reduce the duplication of kitchens, cooking equipment, staffing and storage facilities across individual schools. However, the pilot’s assessment will determine the actual savings. The project also connects school feeding with local agricultural production. The kitchen purchases fresh produce from agricultural cooperatives representing approximately 1,000 smallholder farmers in the surrounding region. Structured purchasing agreements are intended to give farmers a reliable market for their harvests. The arrangement also provides schools with locally grown ingredients. This is another distinction in Rwanda’s approach. Rather than relying solely on large commercial suppliers, the project is designed to link public food procurement directly to smallholder farmers and rural communities. School gardens form another part of the programme. They supplement food supplies while giving students practical lessons in nutrition and food production. Japan’s Shokuiku, or food and nutrition education, similarly treats school meals as an opportunity to teach children about healthy diets, food production and the value of local ingredients. The Rwamagana project follows a partnership agreement signed between the Government of Rwanda and Solid’Africa in November 2023. Solid’Africa previously developed centralised clean-cooking systems for public hospitals in Kigali, and other referral regional hospitals. The school kitchen extends that approach to the education sector. Supported by catalytic funding from The Rockefeller Foundation, the facility will serve as a testing ground for the model. Unlike Japan and South Korea, which have operated nationwide school feeding systems for decades, Rwanda is starting with a limited pilot. The Rwamagana facility serves 15,014 students and 266 teachers, providing an opportunity to assess the model before expanding it. Government officials and technical partners will monitor its performance over the coming school terms. The assessment will cover energy efficiency, meal delivery logistics and the cost of preparing each meal. The findings will inform decisions on whether to establish additional regional kitchen hubs across Rwanda. Save my name, email, and website in this browser for the next time I comment.

title: 15 Songs Like Karol G’s “BbY WOW” for Latin Pop and Dancehall Fans - RouteNote
content: If you love “BbY WOW” by Karol G, Judeline and rusowsky, start with ROSALÍA, Bad Gyal, Feid, Nina Sky and Tainy. Those artists capture different parts of the recording’s appeal. Some combine Latin pop with dancehall rhythms. Others create dreamy alternative R&B or use electronic production to make melancholy songs feel suitable for a club. “BbY WOW” is particularly interesting because it combines those approaches. The song has become one of 2026’s biggest international Latin hits, reaching the top of Billboard’s Global 200 and Global Excl. U.S. charts. The production draws from the Coolie Dance riddim, a Jamaican dancehall instrumental that helped define several early-2000s club hits. If the song sounds familiar, there’s a good reason. Here are fifteen recommendations for listeners who want to explore its musical influences. But the song itself explores feelings connected with a relationship that hasn’t completely disappeared from memory. The combination feels contemporary, but the rhythmic foundation reaches back more than twenty years. Released in 2004, “Move Ya Body” uses the same Coolie Dance riddim associated with “BbY WOW”. The recording combines R&B vocals with a dancehall rhythm. The rhythmic relationship is immediately recognisable, even though the production and vocal personalities are different. “DESPECHÁ” combines an energetic Caribbean-influenced rhythm with lyrics about moving beyond romantic disappointment. The emotional situation is closely related to “BbY WOW”. The narrator is still processing complicated feelings. ROSALÍA’s recording is brighter and more direct, making it an excellent addition to the same playlist. An essential connection with Spanish dancehall-influenced pop. That creates an interesting connection with “BbY WOW”, where the music is danceable but the romantic feelings aren’t entirely happy. For the more experimental side of the collaboration. One of the strongest recommendations for emotional contrast. Tainy’s production combines contemporary Latin rhythms with a distinctive melodic atmosphere. Julieta Venegas and Bad Bunny bring different vocal perspectives. The result is intimate and danceable simultaneously. It’s particularly suitable for listeners who enjoy songs where romantic disappointment exists inside sophisticated electronic production. An essential recording from Karol G’s own catalogue. The song combines a warm tropical rhythm with romantic longing. It’s brighter and more openly celebratory than “BbY WOW”. But the relationship between its emotional message and rhythmic energy is similar. It’s an excellent introduction to Karol G’s ability to move between different Latin musical styles. Featuring The Weeknd, “LA FAMA” combines Latin rhythmic influences with atmospheric R&B vocals. It’s less obviously dancehall-oriented than “BbY WOW”. But the song’s dark romantic atmosphere makes it a useful recommendation for listeners who prefer the more melancholy elements of the collaboration. Rusowsky’s music frequently incorporates experimental electronic textures and understated vocals. “malibU” offers a way to explore his individual musical personality beyond the international chart collaboration. Listeners interested in the unusual vocal processing and atmospheric production of “BbY WOW” should find this direction rewarding. Another important connection with early-2000s Caribbean club music. “Whine Up” combines electronic pop with dancehall influences. The production is energetic and designed for movement. It’s considerably more aggressive than “BbY WOW”, but the rhythmic relationship makes it a natural recommendation. “Efecto” has a hypnotic rhythm and an atmospheric vocal performance. The production creates a feeling of movement without becoming excessively busy. It’s particularly suitable for listeners who enjoy the late-night club atmosphere surrounding Karol G’s recording. Rauw Alejandro combines Latin pop with funk and electronic influences. “Todo de Ti” has an infectious rhythm and polished production. It doesn’t have the same melancholy character as “BbY WOW”, but its melodic accessibility makes it an excellent addition to a wider Latin dance-pop playlist. Nathy Peluso combines Latin influences with an expressive vocal performance and a strong rhythmic arrangement. It’s a useful discovery for listeners interested in performers who move beyond conventional reggaeton production. The production combines Latin-pop vocals with a familiar house-inspired musical idea. This is particularly suitable for listeners who enjoy “BbY WOW” primarily as club music rather than as a romantic song. “TQG” combines two distinctive Colombian vocal personalities with contemporary Latin production. Its message focuses more strongly on confidence after romantic disappointment. That creates an interesting emotional progression from “BbY WOW”. Both recordings demonstrate how Karol G combines mainstream pop accessibility with personal storytelling. Latin pop and dancehall are the strongest descriptions. The recording also incorporates reggaeton, alternative R&B and electronic-pop influences. The Coolie Dance rhythmic foundation is particularly significant. title: Karol G’s Plunging Celia Kritharioti Lace-up Dress Goes Off-Shoulder at Latin Grammys - AOL.com
content: Colombian superstar Karol G delivered a masterclass in bridal-inspired glamour. She stepped out at the 27th Latin Grammy Awards on November 12, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas. The post on Instagram showed the look that balanced romantic softness with a dose of drama. It let a lace-up corset bodice and a slipping neckline do the talking. Karol G wore an ivory gown by Greek designer Celia Kritharioti, defined by a ruched tulle corset bodice with lace-up detailing running down the front. At first glance, the dress appeared soft and ethereal, but the low, off-the-shoulder neckline that slipped down her arms gave the silhouette a daring edge, thus keeping the focus on her shoulders and décolletage. Long sleeves in gathered tulle added a romantic touch. The fitted shape hugged her frame through the waist and hips before the dress opened at the knee into a mermaid skirt of layered tulle with a train. The contrast between the structured top and the airy skirt created a balanced, sculpted effect that elongated her figure. The styling leaned intentionally soft. Karol G wore her long hair loose in glossy waves, in a slightly lighter blonde shade than usual, reinforcing the romantic feel of the gown. Her makeup followed the same philosophy, with a natural, radiant finish that complemented rather than competed with the dress. Accessories were kept minimal, which allowed the dress to remain front and centre. Per the post, Flor de María shoes peeked out from beneath the tulle, adding a subtle finishing touch. The look marked a departure for the singer, who usually works in body-con silhouettes and streetwear. It also fit the night’s bridalcore moment, with Rosalía, Anitta and Mon Laferte among those who arrived in white. It was a big evening for Karol G, who is among the night’s most-nominated artists with seven nominations and was scheduled to perform. Karol G’s Latin Grammys look worked because of its balance of softness and structure. title: Chennai voter count up 21,403 as per draft SSR - The New Indian Express
content: CHENNAI: The number of voters in the city has risen a tad from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) level, with the draft roll released on Thursday as part of the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027 putting the electorate at 29,14,908. This is 21,403 more than the 28,93,505 electors recorded on April 6, 2026. However, the city remains nearly 10.9 lakh short of the 40,04,694 names on its rolls recorded before the SIR exercise. District Election Officer and Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G S Sameeran released the draft roll at Ripon Building in the presence of representatives of recognised political parties.  January 1, 2027, is the qualifying date for the revision. The draft published in December 2025 had left out 14.25 lakh names from the city’s rolls, a 35.6% cut, the highest among Tamil Nadu’s districts, bringing the electorate down to 25,79,676. The final roll on February 23, 2026, climbed back to 28,30,936 after a net addition of 2.51 lakh during claims and objections, but even that left the city 29.3% below its pre-SIR strength. Anna Nagar lost the largest share of its electorate in the SIR draft at 42.2%, while Velachery lost the most names at 1,27,521. The final roll narrowed these gaps but barely with Thousand Lights ending 35.43% lesser than its pre-SIR strength and Anna Nagar 35.31%, the highest in the city. Even Perambur, which recorded the highest additions during claims and objections at 24,142, finished 25.12% below its count before the SIR was taken up. In the draft-stage deletion data, Anna Nagar had 1,08,828 names marked as shifted and just one as absent, while Harbour had 60,258 marked shifted and none absent. A TNIE analysis in January had found these two categories were used arbitrarily and interchangeably, particularly in urban areas. Women continue to outnumber men on the rolls with the draft carrying 15,09,040 women against 14,04,968 men besides 900 third-gender voters. Since April 6, the number of women has risen by 12,119, against an increase of 9,252 men and 32 third-gender voters. The continuous revision between April 6 and October 31 added 34,999 names and deleted 13,596 and accounted for the net rise of 21,403. The additions comprised 15,762 men, 19,197 women and 40 third-gender voters while the deletions comprised 6,510 men, 7,078 women and eight third-gender voters. Velachery gained the most since April 6, adding 2,181 electors, with Virugambakkam next at 2,038, Perambur at 1,843 and Kolathur at 1,767. Perambur remains the city’s largest constituency with 2,28,139 electors and Harbour the smallest with 1,20,852. Polling stations have come down from 4,079 to 4,071. The draft roll includes 46,200 electors aged 18-19 and 28,159 aged above 85. It has 12,805 voters with disabilities and 531 service voters. Claims and objections can be filed until December 11. Special camps will be held at all polling stations on November 21, 22 and 29, from 10 am to 5 pm, for inclusion of eligible voters and corrections to entries. title: 2026 Global Alternatives Survey: The LP View - Goldman Sachs Asset Management

Despite geopolitical uncertainty, inflation concerns and liquidity constraints, institutional investors remain committed to private markets. Most respondents view opportunities across private equity, private credit and infrastructure as equal to or better than last year, and more than a third expect to deploy more capital. As a result, investors are not retreating from private markets, but becoming more selective in how they allocate capital, manage liquidity and choose investment managers. Many remain under allocated to private markets, particularly private credit and infrastructure, suggesting continued room for capital deployment. While slower distributions continue to constrain new commitments, investor appetite remains resilient. In response, investors are placing greater emphasis on liquidity management, with secondaries and co-investments becoming increasingly important components of portfolio construction. Manager quality remains a key driver of capital allocation decisions, with investors increasingly focused on underwriting discipline, specialist expertise and differentiated investment approaches. At the same time, respondents identified artificial intelligence as the leading force expected to reshape the private markets industry over the next five years. Together, these trends suggest investors are raising the bar for manager selection, seeking firms with both proven investment capabilities and the ability to adapt to structural changes across private markets. title: GS E&C Repays 112.6 Billion Won in Debt for Battery Recycling Unit - Seoul Economic Daily
content: Construction Firm Takes Over Mortgage Rights Held by Korea Development Bank GS E&C (006360.KS) said on the 13th that it will repay the remaining debt and interest its subsidiary Energy Materials borrowed from Korea Development Bank. The payment totals 112.551 billion won ($76.5 million) and will be made the same day. The company said the repayment gives it the right to seek reimbursement from Energy Materials and transfers to GS E&C the existing mortgage rights held by Korea Development Bank. Energy Materials, established in 2020, had operated a plant extracting battery raw material metals from used batteries. It suspended operations last month after struggling with difficulties in securing raw materials and deteriorating profitability. "By repaying the remaining borrowings and interest of our subsidiary Energy Materials, we will preemptively block financial risk and minimize the financial impact by securing reimbursement rights and collateral rights," a GS E&C official said. title: John Summit Drops Official Remix of Karol G’s ‘BbY WOW’ - EDMTunes
content:
John Summit has officially released his remix of Karol G‘s ‘BbY WOW,’ out now via Experts Only/Bichota Records. The Chicago-born, Miami-based producer first tested the edit live during a September show in Bogotá, Colombia, reworking one of the year’s biggest Latin pop crossover hits into something built for his own tech house sets. Since that first run-out, the remix has stuck around as a fixture of Summit’s live shows, generating the kind of crowd reaction that usually pushes an unofficial edit toward a proper release. That’s exactly what happened here, with Karol G’s camp and Bichota Records signing off on an official version rather than leaving it to bootleg YouTube rips and festival set recordings. The timing lines up with another notable crossover moment between the two artists. Last week, Summit made a surprise appearance at Karol G’s release celebration for No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto in Mexico City, joining her onstage to perform the remix together for the first time. The pairing of Summit’s club-oriented production with the original’s Latin pop and reggaetón DNA underscored just how far his sound has traveled beyond the house and techno circuit he built his name in. The celebration included a full live performance of Karol G’s 14-track album and streamed globally on TikTok LIVE, reportedly becoming one of the platform’s most-watched livestreams to date. The remix arrives in the middle of the most expansive tour run of Summit’s career. He’s currently crisscrossing North American arenas in support of his album CTRL ESCAPE, released back in April, a project that fuses tech house with dubstep, drum & bass, and other influences Summit has been slowly folding into his sets over the past couple years. Dates on the current leg include stops at Chicago’s United Center, Miami’s Kaseya Center, and a sold-out show at Brooklyn’s Barclays Center on November 28. Once the North American run wraps, Summit heads overseas for European dates before closing out the year with festival stops in Australia and New Zealand. The tour follows a run of milestones that have defined Summit’s 2026, including a hometown headline set at Lollapalooza, his debut Ibiza residency at [UNVRS], and the return of his Experts Only Festival to New York, which pulled in 60,000 fans across two days at Randall’s Island. Summit’s label, Experts Only, has become the banner under which he’s staged everything from Tennessee hill takeovers to snow-covered events in Vail and Tahoe. A former CPA, Summit has built a catalog that includes over three billion global streams, two number one U.S. dance radio hits, and eleven Top 10 entries on the Billboard Hot Electronic/Dance Songs chart. His 2024 debut album Comfort In Chaos explored themes of vice and virtue, while CTRL ESCAPE reframes that same tension around the push and pull between the 9-to-5 grind and the release of the rave. title: Study finds European motorcycle industry generates £30 billion in GDP - Visordown
content: An Oxford Economics study has found that the European motorcycle industry generates around £30 billion in GDP. A newly published study has found that the European motorcycle industry generates almost £30 billion in GDP. Motorcycling in Europe feels constantly under pressure to justify itself. In the UK, October saw year-to-year growth for the motorcycle industry of over 10 per cent in terms of registrations, yet MCIA CEO Tony Campbell said after the figures were published that the UK government still does not realise the true value and significance of the country’s motorcycle sector.’ In Europe, Antonio Perlot, the secretary general of the manufacturers’ association, ACEM, has conducted a study with Oxford Economics into the impact of the motorcycle industry on the European economy. The findings of the study are stark: 481,600 jobs and €35 billion (£29 billion) in GDP, a popular measure of a country’s economic strength. €26 billion of that overall GDP contribution comes from making, selling, and repairing motorcycles, while €5 billion comes from equipment like helmets and other riding gear, and €2.7 billion comes from racing and other events. The study also found that the trade gap – the difference between imports and exports – for European motorcycling had doubled since 2019, from a €1 billion gap to €2 billion, in favour of imports. It’s therefore not only a study that shows the importance of the European motorcycle industry to the region itself, but also highlights the risks it faces at present and therefore the importance of political support for it. The study was presented by ACEM at EICMA, where Perlot said it gives a “complete picture” of the value of motorcycling to Europe. “This study gives us a complete picture of what motorcycling brings to Europe: €35 billion in value, almost half a million jobs and real benefits for the way people move in cities,” said Antonio Perlot, ACEM Secretary General. “But these figures cannot be taken for granted. To stay competitive, European manufacturers need fair and reciprocal access to global markets, motorcycles fully integrated in urban mobility planning and, above all, conditions supporting manufacturers’ continued investment in Europe.” Mariano Roman, President of Confindustria ANCMA, added: “These figures confirm the value of an industry that creates jobs, skills and innovation, and in which Italy is one of Europe’s leading players. “EICMA is its global point of reference: the place where the motorcycle industry presents its future and engages with markets, the public and institutions. Bringing this debate here means linking the sector’s economic and social value to the choices needed to sustain it. “Growth in registrations does not automatically translate into higher production and profitability: to keep investing and innovating in Europe, we need clear and proportionate rules, reciprocity in trade and full recognition of two-wheelers in mobility policies.” Stay up to speed with the latest motorcycling news and analysis, delivered straight to your inbox. Total non-interest revenues were $14.91 billion, up 32% year over year. The increase reflected higher investment banking revenues, investment management revenues, commissions and fees, and market-making revenues, partially offset by lower other principal transactions revenues. Net interest income was $3.77 billion, down 2% from the prior-year quarter. On the cost side, operating expenses were $11.31 billion, up 20% from the prior-year quarter. Management attributed the increase primarily to significantly higher transaction-based expenses and higher compensation and benefits expenses, reflecting improved operating performance. Even with higher costs, Goldman's efficiency ratio declined 180 basis points to 60.5% for the quarter. Provision for credit losses was $368 million, up from $339 million in the year-ago quarter, primarily reflecting impairments related to wholesale loans. The Asset & Wealth Management business generated net revenues of $5.05 billion, up 14% year over year. The increase primarily reflected significantly higher management and other fees, driven by higher average assets under supervision, and higher incentive fees from fund distributions. These positives were partially offset by lower investments and private banking, and lending revenues. Total assets under supervision increased to a record $4.10 trillion, reflecting $83 billion in total net inflows and $97 billion in long-term net inflows during the quarter. The Global Banking & Markets business generated net revenues of $13.46 billion, up 32% year over year. Growth was driven by significantly higher Equities revenues and increased investment banking fees, while FICC revenues remained essentially unchanged. Equities benefited from significantly higher financing and intermediation revenues, while investment banking fees were supported by higher advisory, equity underwriting and debt underwriting revenues. The Platform Solutions business reported net revenues of $170 million, down 72% from the year-ago quarter. The decline primarily reflected net markdowns related to the Apple Card loan portfolio, which had previously been transferred to held for sale. Goldman ended the third quarter with total assets of $2.18 trillion, up from $2.13 trillion at the end of the second quarter, while deposits were $568 billion compared with $558 billion in the previous quarter. title: Tripura Inducts 3 Senior TPS Officers into IPS, DGP G.S. Rao Confers Insignia at Ceremony - Indian Masterminds
content: Home » News » Bureaucracy News » Tripura Inducts 3 Senior TPS Officers into IPS, DGP G.S. Rao Confers Insignia at Ceremony AGARTALA: Tripura Police has received a boost to its senior leadership with the induction of three Tripura Police Service (TPS) officers into the Indian Police Service (IPS). The newly promoted officers are Kishore Debbarma, Rajib Nag and Rajib Sengupta, who have been allocated to the Tripura cadre following their elevation under the prescribed promotion framework. To mark the occasion, a ceremonial piping event was organised at the Police Headquarters on Thursday. During the ceremony, Tripura Director General of Police (DGP) G.S. Rao, a 1999-batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of the Tripura cadre, formally adorned the three officers with the IPS insignia. The event was attended by senior police officials and colleagues, who congratulated the officers on their elevation to one of the country’s premier All India Services. The induction marks an important milestone in their careers and recognises their years of service in the Tripura Police. The induction follows a notification issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on November 6, 2026, appointing Kishore Debbarma, Rajib Nag and Rajib Sengupta to the Indian Police Service under the Select List of 2025. The appointments have been made in accordance with the provisions of the Indian Police Service (Recruitment) Rules, 1954, and the Indian Police Service (Appointment by Promotion) Regulations, 1955. Under the promotion process, eligible officers of the State Police Service are considered for induction into the IPS through the prescribed selection and appointment framework. With this notification, all three officers have formally entered the IPS and have been allocated to the Tripura cadre. Read also: Tripura DGP Charge: Why 1999-Batch GS Rao Was Given Additional Responsibility Despite Senior IPS Officers As part of their induction into the Indian Police Service, all three officers will undergo a one-year probation period along with mandatory induction training, as prescribed under the applicable IPS regulations. The training programme is intended to familiarise promoted officers with the administrative, operational and leadership responsibilities associated with the IPS. It will also prepare them to handle higher-level responsibilities within the police administration and strengthen their understanding of the broader functioning of the All India Service. The Ministry of Home Affairs notification has clarified that the appointments will remain subject to the final outcome of the pending Special Leave Petition (Civil) Nos. 19765–19767 of 2015. The matter relates to the case of State of Tripura and Others versus Jayanta Chakraborty and Others. Accordingly, the induction of the three officers is subject to the final decision in the pending legal proceedings. The elevation of Kishore Debbarma, Rajib Nag and Rajib Sengupta is being viewed as recognition of their service and contributions to law enforcement in Tripura. Their induction into the Indian Police Service is expected to strengthen the senior leadership structure of the state police and enhance its administrative and operational capabilities. The ceremonial event at Police Headquarters marked a proud occasion for the Tripura Police fraternity, highlighting the promotion opportunities available to State Police Service officers and their progression into the country’s premier policing cadre. The GS Diagoras Volleyball Department is taking an important step to raise social awareness, demonstrating in practice that sport is not limited to competitive results but can be a powerful means of contributing to society and promoting solidarity.
