title: NBA Power Rankings: Spurs rise, plus the best newcomer on all 30 teams - ESPN
content:
The NBA season is starting to take shape as the holiday window approaches. The San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are once again surging early, but their Western Conference counterparts the Los Angeles Lakers have arguably been the most impressive team in a competitive West. The Lakers are fueled by Luka Doncic's historic start, which has featured 39.3 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game. In the East, the new-look Philadelphia 76ers seem like they've been playing together for years, as LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have hit the ground running with their new teammates. They're tailed tightly by their offseason trade partners, the Boston Celtics, who seemingly haven't missed a beat with new faces around Jayson Tatum. In this week's Power Rankings, our ESPN insiders rank where each team stands, per usual, and also highlight each team's best newcomer over the first few weeks of the season. Which players are vaulting their teams up the standings? Find out in this week's Power Rankings. Jump to a team:
ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE
DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND
LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN
NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX
POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS Next games: @ CHI (Nov. 11), vs. GS (Nov. 13), @ UTAH (Nov. 15) Drafted 26th in 2026, Tarris Reed Jr. knew earning minutes as a rookie in San Antonio would be difficult, even after he gave French phenom Victor Wembanyama buckets, according to sources, in the early days of open gym over the summer. Reed is averaging just 5.3 minutes per game, but the Spurs' brass has been impressed with the rookie's preparedness every time his number is called. San Antonio is thin at center, and veteran backup Luke Kornet has struggled. That could lead to more minutes for Reed as the season progresses. -- Mike C. Wright Next games: @ MIL (Nov. 11), @ PHX (Nov. 15), vs. CHA (Nov. 17) After recording one of the most memorable debuts imaginable -- when he scored 26 points on a perfect 12-for-12 from the field in a win -- Kessler has continued to have a major impact. The 7-2 center has been durable, playing in all 12 of L.A.'s games, and averaging a career high in points (14.9) while shooting 69.1% from the field, with 10.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game. He has also played north of 30 minutes per game while averaging only 2.9 fouls, which is paramount for a Lakers roster without a go-to big man to back him up.  -- Dave McMenamin Next games: @ POR (Nov. 11), @ LAC (Nov. 13), @ SAC (Nov. 15) Rookie center Aday Mara, selected with the No. 12 pick courtesy of the LA Clippers, has made an instant impact in Oklahoma City. The 7-foot-3 big man entered the league as an elite rim protector, ranking fifth in the NBA with 1.9 blocks per game. Mara also has a soft touch in the paint and intriguing potential as a passer. He ranks fifth among rookies in rebounding (5.9 per game) and is also averaging 8.1 points on 62.5% shooting over 19 minutes per game. -- Tim MacMahon Next games: vs. TOR (Nov. 12), vs. IND (Nov. 15), @ BKN (Nov. 16) Brown has said that this is Tyrese Maxey's team, but as of late, it's starting to look like his, as well. He had his best stretch as a Sixer on the team's recent road trip, scoring 30 points in a win over Detroit and 29 points in a win over the Chicago Bulls. "He's something we really needed," Maxey said. -- Kris Rhim Next games: @ TOR (Nov. 11), vs. DAL (Nov. 15), vs. ORL (Nov. 16) George set the tone for what this season would be on opening night, breaking the franchise record for the most points in a debut with 38. Since then, he has remained a seamless fit in Boston, becoming one of the team's best wing defenders and a reliable second option on offense as the Celtics have jumped out to the second-best record in the East. "On and off the court he's been great," coach Joe Mazzulla said. -- Rhim Next games: vs. DAL (Nov. 12), vs. CHI (Nov. 14), vs. POR (Nov. 16) The Timberwolves should be ecstatic with the early returns from their summer trade for Ball, who quickly forged a dynamic partnership with Anthony Edwards. Even after Edwards was sidelined by knee surgery, Ball has kept Minnesota's offense in the top 10 and is on pace to be the franchise's first player to average at least six assists since D'Angelo Russell in 2022-23. Meanwhile, the Hornets' offensive efficiency has plummeted from fifth last season to 30th this season after trading Ball in June. No takebacks. -- Ben Golliver Next games: vs. GS (Nov. 11), vs. UTAH (Nov. 13), @ WAS (Nov. 15) Veteran guard Marcus Smart is not only reliable for coach Ime Udoka but also familiar with him from their time together with the Celtics. Most of all, Smart gives the Rockets another steady ball handler and tenacious defender capable of starting whenever Fred VanVleet is forced to rest on the second night of back-to-backs, as he continues to recover from last year's ACL surgery. A former NBA Defensive Player of the Year, Smart plays with the intelligence and toughness that Udoka covets and provides veteran leadership alongside VanVleet and Kevin Durant. -- Wright Next games: @ WAS (Nov. 12), @ MIA (Nov. 14), @ SAS (Nov. 17) It was a bit of a slow start for Collins, who signed as a free agent to replace veteran Tobias Harris. Collins fits more what the Pistons want to be, with his athleticism and shooting as complements to Jalen Duren's interior presence. However, with Duren out with a hamstring injury, it forced Collins to be paired with Paul Reed, which has been a bit clunky. When J.B. Bickerstaff removed Reed from the first five and went small against the Wizards, it opened things up for Collins -- he scored a season-high 24 points and added 10 rebounds in a 122-111 win Monday night. -- Vincent Goodwill Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 11), @ SAS (Nov. 13), @ NO (Nov. 16) During one of his unfiltered livestreams this summer, Lendeborg -- the outspoken No. 11 pick -- predicted he would average around 15 points, six rebounds and four assists as a rookie. It felt overly ambitious at the time. It appears he might've been shorting himself. Through his first 11 games, Lendeborg is averaging 21.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and four assists. The scoring punch has been particularly surprising and important for the surging 8-3 Warriors. Lendeborg is making better than 44% of his 5.5 attempted 3s per game and has gained enough trust from Steve Kerr that the coach is putting the basketball in the rookie's hands to make decisions down the stretch of close games. -- Anthony Slater Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 11), @ IND (Nov. 13), @ TOR (Nov. 15) At times it has appeared like Drummond has been out of place, with Mike Brown pulling Drummond abruptly in the middle of games for not getting back on defense and trying his hand with James Wiseman instead. But one thing that cannot be denied is Drummond's effect on the glass. The Knicks were supposed to suffer a drop-off as one of the best offensive rebounding teams after Mitchell Robinson departed to Boston. But per 36 minutes, Drummond has averaged over eight offensive rebounds to help the Knicks remain a top-three team in that category. And Brown has complemented Drummond's screen-roll defense recently, noting his physicality. -- Goodwill Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 11), @ SAC (Nov. 13), @ MIN (Nov. 16) Portland's best newcomer is actually an old friend in Lillard, who is doing his best to make Rip City forget that he was traded to the Bucks in 2023 and missed last season with an Achilles injury. Lillard, 36, is averaging 19.4 points and 4.4 assists, and he has made fast friends with All-Star wing Deni Avdija. The Blazers boast an excellent plus-9.4 net rating when Avdija and Lillard, their two leading scorers, share the court. -- Golliver Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 14), vs. PHX (Nov. 16) The Nuggets remain in a perpetual search for lineup combinations that can survive in the minutes either Nikola Jokic or the scorching Jamal Murray are off the floor. Through nine games, they're minus-15 in Jokic's bench time and minus-29 in Murray's. But within that, in their latest search for depth pieces after Peyton Watson's departure this past summer, they've received encouraging contributions from Brazile and Bryce Hopkins -- both second-rounders from the 2026 draft. Brazile is a 6-10 wing with a 7-4 wingspan, flashing early as a rebounder and a defensive disruptor in a few of Denver's wins. He's averaging 20.3 minutes, a number that might rise as the season progresses. -- Slater Next games: vs. DEN (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 13), vs. @BKN (Nov. 14) Rookie Cameron Boozer, the third pick of the 2026 draft, is already surprising some opponents with his unexpected agility and scoring prowess. "I had no clue he could move the way he moves, also that he could shoot the way he shoots," said Golden State center Draymond Green on "The Draymond Green Show" podcast. With Isaiah Stewart out due to a right knee bone bruise, Boozer is also having to showcase his versatility by sliding over from his natural power forward spot to center. "We are featuring him in a lot of different sets," Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said. -- Wright With the Hawks' offense struggling early in the season, coach Quin Snyder inserted the rookie Flemings into the starting lineup and moved veteran CJ McCollum to a reserve role. The Hawks went on to win three out of the four games with Flemings as starter while ranking fifth in offense. Something to pay attention to is whether Snyder trusts Flemings to close games. In the past four games, he ranks eighth in minutes per game in the fourth quarter.  -- Bobby Marks Next games: @ MIN (Nov. 12), @ CLE (Nov. 14), @ BOS (Nov. 15) The Mavericks took a flier on Risacher when they acquired him in the three-way trade that sent Luguentz Dort to Atlanta, hoping they could develop the former No. 1 pick into a quality role player. The 6-9 Risacher has impressed with his defensive activity as a reserve, averaging 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. Coach Dusty May is comfortable giving Risacher the assignment of guarding elite scorers across multiple positions. His defense on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Kevin Durant helped the Mavs pull off wins over the Thunder and Rockets. -- MacMahon ESPN Analytics has unveiled its new NBA Trade Lab, an interactive web app for fans to build, save and vote on mock trades. Can you build the perfectly balanced trade that fans of all teams involved would accept?
• Build your own trades here
• More NBA coverage Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 11), @ MIA (Nov. 13), vs. DAL (Nov. 14) Headline acquisition Peyton Watson is still struggling to find his footing in Cleveland, but Thomas, picked 34th in the 2026 draft, has been a pleasant surprise for the Cavaliers. The rookie guard shone at summer league and has carried over that performance to games that count, averaging 13 points and hitting 48% of his 3s so far. After starting the season with three DNPs in Cleveland's first five games, Thomas has quickly worked his way into playing 20-plus minutes every night. -- Zach Kram Next games: vs. BOS (Nov. 11), @ PHI (Nov. 12), vs. NYK (Nov. 15) This should be going to Kawhi Leonard, who returned to Toronto in an offseason trade, but he has played only two games this season while sidelined with soreness in his left knee. The reality for the Raptors is that no newcomer has made a significant impact this season, but Graves, the team's first-round pick, has been the best of the team's additions, which include veteran Kyle Anderson and rookie Jaden Bradley. He has reached double digits once this season, scoring 11 points in a loss to Minnesota, and has largely played a depth role. -- Rhim Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 13), vs. DET (Nov. 14), vs. HOU (Nov. 16) Even with the Heat's early-season struggles, it would be almost malpractice if we left Antetokounmpo off the list. After playing a career-low 36 games last season with Milwaukee, Antetokounmpo has appeared in all 10 games this season. The former MVP has scored 25 points or more in seven games and is on pace to average the most rebounds in his career since 2019-20. He is currently averaging a career-high 3.7 offensive rebounds. -- Marks Next games: @ IND (Nov. 11), vs. DET (Nov. 12), vs. HOU (Nov. 15) The 10-time All-Star counts as a newcomer, right? He technically joined the Wizards last February but didn't play a game for them until this season. All he has done with his new team is average 25.7 points and 9.7 rebounds this season. Washington is 4-5 when Davis plays and 0-2 when he doesn't, including a 39-point shellacking in Oklahoma City without the star big man on the court. -- Kram Next games: vs. BKN (Nov. 11), vs. MEM (Nov. 13), vs. DEN (Nov. 14) Coach Jamahl Mosley has largely relied on familiar faces while juggling his rotation due to injuries. Believe it or not, New Orleans' top eight scorers are all returning members of last year's 26-win team. Watford, a journeyman forward who joined the Pelicans on a minimum contract this summer, has worked his way into Mosley's rotation by averaging 7.2 points and 3.5 rebounds off the bench over the past six games. Meanwhile, Bennedict Mathurin, a 2022 lottery pick who inked a two-year, $15.4 million deal with New Orleans in free agency, is averaging a career-low 15.0 minutes per game. -- Golliver "The Hoop Collective" podcast, hosted by Brian Windhorst, releases new shows every Monday, Wednesday and Friday during the NBA season.
• Listen to the latest episodes Next games: vs. CHA (Nov. 12), vs. LAL (Nov. 15), @ DEN (Nov. 16) This year's Suns team, which ranks last in the league in rebounds per game, would be in even worse shape on the boards if not for Bridges securing a career-best 7.8 caroms per game -- two more than he averaged for the Charlotte Hornets last season. The 6-7 forward is also putting up 15.8 points, 3.2 assists and a career-high 1.2 steals per game. After starting the season 1-5, Phoenix won two out of its past three games, with Bridges averaging 9.3 rebounds during that stretch. -- McMenamin Next games: vs. WAS (Nov. 11), vs. NYK (Nov. 13), @ PHI (Nov. 15) Injuries have interrupted Zubac's total impact in his new home, but he played one of his best games of the season against the Mavericks this week, despite a modest box score -- 16 points on 5-of-7 shooting, but the team was a plus-6 while he was in the game. In spurts, he has shown there is room for more, especially as the Pacers get accustomed to his game while they await Tyrese Haliburton's return to the lineup. -- Jamal Collier Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 12), @ LAC (Nov. 15), @ LAL (Nov. 17) Allen is averaging 15.3 points for the Hornets while making 47% of his 3-point tries. Charlotte ranks 28th in 3-point percentage as a team, but that's not Allen's fault. He ranks second in individual 3-point percentage (sandwiched between Jamal Murray and Stephen Curry) out of 77 players with at least 50 attempts. -- Kram Next games: @ UTAH (Nov. 11), vs. MIL (Nov. 13), @ BOS (Nov. 16) Da Silva is not considered a newcomer since he was drafted in the 2024 first round. But with the injury to Paolo Banchero, Da Silva is averaging career highs in minutes (30.5) and points (15.1). He is also shooting 40% from 3. Da Silva was a new face to the Magic's starting five on Saturday night as he made his first start of the season in a loss to Golden State. -- Marks Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 13), vs. CHA (Nov. 15), vs. UTAH (Nov. 17) The 6-5 guard, selected with the No. 5 pick out of Illinois, ranks fifth in 3-point percentage (39.0%) among rookies with at least 30 attempts. He has also found a way to generate points at the line, ranking second in total free throw attempts and second in free throw percentage (86.5%) among rookies with at least 30 trips to the line. As the Clippers begin their rebuild after the lackluster Kawhi Leonard-Paul George era, Wagler's development should be priority No. 1 for the franchise this season. -- McMenamin Next games: @ NO (Nov. 11), @ MEM (Nov. 14), vs. PHI (Nov. 16) It has been hit or miss for Randle so far this season -- he has had bouts of being the most consistent Net on a team full of developing guards. He has had to create his own offense, which he might prefer, as Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Demin are also battling injuries. He and Michael Porter Jr. can only play together so much because their styles clash, and on some nights like Sunday against Dallas, he'll be a minus-33 in a 130-93 loss. He's a proud veteran in a tough situation -- not an ideal one -- and the Nets have to find ways to maximize him on this ill-fitting team. -- Goodwill Wednesday, Nov. 18

He has had his first three 20-point performances in the Jazz's past three games. Peterson has averaged 24 points on 51.9% shooting from the floor (11-of-24 on 3s) over those three games. -- MacMahon Next games: @ SAS (Nov. 11), vs. ATL (Nov. 13), @ MIN (Nov. 14) There haven't been many bright spots for the Bulls so far, but Wilson looks like he belongs. The early returns are strong at 19 points and six rebounds per game, yet his potential is tantalizing. He attacks the basket with intent to dunk everything, and his highlights on defense are eye-popping. Wilson isn't used to losing frequently, so with the Bulls in position to keep racking up L's, Chicago is already trying to manage his body language and effort. Tiago Splitter benched him last week against the Knicks because he noticed him getting down after missing some shots. Still, despite the growing pains, Wilson is easily the team's best newcomer. -- Collier Next games: vs. LAL (Nov. 11), @ ORL (Nov. 13), vs. ATL (Nov. 15) Burries has already replaced Ryan Rollins in the Bucks' starting lineup, and he has easily been the biggest bright spot during a miserable start to the year in Milwaukee. He has come out the gates as a great rebounder, and since moving to the starting lineup, he's averaging 13.0 points, 8.0 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 29 minutes. As the Bucks' season continues to slip away, Burries should get even more opportunities. -- Collier The No. 7 pick has opened his career with 20 or more shot attempts in 10 consecutive games, the longest streak for a rookie since Wilt Chamberlain (19 games) back in 1959. It hasn't all been cloaked in inefficiency, either. Acuff has made 45% or more of those shots in five of the past six games, showing greater comfort and passing willingness. title: Want to invest in government bonds? RBI's 6.94% GS 2036 auction opens on November 13: How to apply - Upstox
content: 3 min read | Updated on November 11, 2026, 09:57 IST RBI will auction its 6.94% GS 2036 bond on November 13. Find out how retail investors can apply through RBI Retail Direct, minimum investment and key details. Government of India securities carry no domestic currency credit risk, according to the RBI, but they are subject to market risk. | Image: Shutterstock. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) will auction the 6.94% Government of India Security 2036 on November 13, 2026. The government plans to raise ₹34,000 crore through the re-issue, with an option to accept an additional subscription of up to ₹2,000 crore. Individual investors can participate through the non-competitive bidding facility on the RBI Retail Direct platform, with a minimum investment of ₹10,000 in face value. The 6.94% GS 2036 will mature on May 11, 2036. Since this is a re-issue, the auction will be price-based and follow the multiple-price method. Maximum investment: ₹2 crore per investor per security per auction Non-competitive bidding window: 10:30 am to 11:00 am Unlike competitive bidders, retail investors do not have to quote a price or yield. They simply specify the face value they wish to purchase. Allotment takes place at the weighted average price emerging from successful competitive bids. The RBI has provided for up to 5% of the notified amount to be allotted to eligible individuals and institutions under this facility. For this auction, that works out to ₹1,700 crore. After opening the account, they can select the eligible security and submit their non-competitive bid during the specified window on November 13. The minimum bid is ₹10,000 in face value, in multiples of ₹10,000 thereafter. The maximum bid is ₹2 crore per investor per security per auction. The actual payment may differ from the face value because the RBI's calculation includes the indicative price, accrued interest and applicable markup. Not necessarily. The 6.94% is the annual coupon rate, not the actual investment yield. For a face value of ₹10,000, the annual coupon interest is ₹694, generally payable in two instalments of ₹347 each, on May 11 and November 11. The actual yield depends on the auction price. Buying above face value generally reduces the effective yield, while buying below face value increases it. title: GS, POSCO join hands for future large-scale AI data center projects - The Korea Times
content: GS Group and POSCO signed a memorandum of understanding Wednesday to partner on AI data center projects. They plan to coordinate materials, equipment and design to reduce construction delays, shorten build times and lower costs, while also exploring ways to improve operating efficiency and pursue overseas projects. GS is developing a data center project in Donghae, Gangwon Province, with a planned capacity of 2.4 gigawatts. GS Group Vice Chairman Hong Soon-ki, right, poses with POSCO CEO Lee Hee-geun after signing a memorandum of understanding on the two sides' cooperation in the artificial intelligence data center sector at GS Tower in Gangnam District, Seoul, Wednesday. Courtesy of GS Group GS Group and POSCO will form a strategic partnership in the artificial intelligence (AI) data center market, combining GS Group's expertise in data center construction and operation with POSCO's high-quality steel materials and technological solutions. GS Group said Wednesday that it has signed a memorandum of understanding  with POSCO on a strategic partnership in the AI data center business. The signing ceremony was attended by GS Group Vice Chairman Hong Soon-ki, POSCO CEO Lee Hee-geun and other executives from both companies. Through the agreement, the two companies plan to minimize delays in the supply of equipment and materials during the construction of large-scale data centers and optimize material selection and design solutions to shorten construction periods and reduce costs. These efforts are expected to facilitate the early operation of data centers and improve their profitability, GS Group said. The agreement also includes practical cooperation to explore ways to reduce operating costs, improve space utilization and enhance the durability of facilities and equipment to strengthen the long-term operational competitiveness of data centers. The two sides will join efforts for global market entry as well, by leveraging the overseas business networks of GS Global and POSCO to identify data center development demands and jointly explore opportunities to supply materials and equipment for overseas projects. “AI data centers require capabilities from various industries to enable stable power supply, rapid construction and efficient operation,” Hong said. “Through this partnership, we will combine GS Group’s data center development capabilities with POSCO’s world-class materials and solutions to explore new growth opportunities in the global AI infrastructure market.” Lee said AI data centers represent a new growth segment that will drive global demand for steel and materials, adding that the two sides will “establish a strong leadership position in the global AI data center market.” GS Group is currently pursuing a 2.4-gigawatt data center project in Donghae, Gangwon Province, through its subsidiary GS AI Infrastructure. In September, the group announced plans to invest approximately 15 trillion won ($11.23 billion) in the first phase of the project and obtained a construction permit for its first 100-megawatt data center in October. POSCO established a new Future Demand Development Office this year to identify business opportunities in AI data center and power grid businesses. The company is also expanding its development of high-value-added steel materials and solutions for data center applications, ranging from structural components to power and cooling equipment.
